source.text: Πρεσβυτέρους οὖν ἐν ὑμῖν παρακαλῶ ὁ συμπρεσβύτερος καὶ μάρτυς τῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ παθημάτων, ὁ καὶ τῆς μελλούσης ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι δόξης κοινωνός, ποιμάνατε τὸ ἐν ὑμῖν ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐπισκοποῦντες μὴ ἀναγκαστῶς ἀλλὰ ἑκουσίως κατὰ θεόν, μηδὲ αἰσχροκερδῶς ἀλλὰ προθύμως, μηδ’ ὡς κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων ἀλλὰ τύποι γινόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου·

records.literal_gloss: Elders therefore among you I exhort, the fellow elder and witness of the of the Christ sufferings, the [one] also of the about to be revealed glory sharer, \v 2 shepherd the among you flock of the God, overseeing not by compulsion but willingly according to God, nor shamefully-for-gain but eagerly, \v 3 nor as lording over the allotted [portions] but examples becoming of the flock;

en.L: So I exhort the elders among you, [I who am] a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and also a sharer in the glory about to be revealed: \v 2 shepherd the flock of God [that is] among you, watching over [it], not by compulsion but voluntarily, according to God, nor for shameful profit but with eagerness, \v 3 nor as lording [it] over the [people] allotted [to you], but becoming examples for the flock.
en.B: So I appeal to the elders among you. I am an elder with you, a witness of the sufferings of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and one who will also share in the glory that is about to be revealed. \v 2 Tend God's flock among you as shepherds do. Take care of it freely, the way God would have it, not because you are forced to; not to make money for yourselves, but gladly and readily. \v 3 Do not rule harshly over the people given into your charge; set an example for the flock instead.
en.R: I am an elder too, and I have something to ask of the elders among you. I am a witness of the sufferings of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and I will also have a share in the glory that God is about to show. \v 2 Care for God's people the way a shepherd cares for a flock of sheep. Watch over them because you want to, not because you have to. That is what God wants. Do not do it to get money, but do it with all your heart. \v 3 Do not be bossy with the people God has given you to look after. Instead, show them by the way you live how they should live.

es.L: Así pues, a los ancianos que hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los exhorto [yo], anciano como ellos y testigo de los sufrimientos {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, y también partícipe de la gloria que va a ser revelada: \v 2 {{plural_you:pastoreen|pastoread}} el rebaño de Dios [que está] entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, velando [por él] no por obligación, sino de buena gana, según Dios; ni por ganancia vergonzosa, sino con entusiasmo; \v 3 ni como quienes dominan sobre los [que se {{plural_you:les|os}} han] asignado, sino llegando a ser ejemplos para el rebaño.
es.B: Por eso hago un llamado a los ancianos que hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Yo también soy anciano, testigo de los sufrimientos {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} y uno que tendrá parte en la gloria que está por revelarse. \v 2 {{plural_you:Pastoreen|Pastoread}} el rebaño de Dios que está entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Cuídenlo|Cuidadlo}} de buena voluntad, tal como Dios desea, y no porque {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} obligados; no para sacar dinero para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos, sino con gusto y disposición. \v 3 No {{plural_you:gobiernen|gobernéis}} con dureza a quienes {{plural_you:les|os}} han sido confiados; más bien, con {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida {{plural_you:den|dad}} ejemplo al rebaño.
es.R: Yo también soy anciano, y tengo algo que pedir a los ancianos que hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Soy testigo de los sufrimientos {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, y también tendré parte en la gloria que Dios está a punto de mostrar. \v 2 {{plural_you:Cuiden|Cuidad}} al pueblo de Dios como un pastor cuida su rebaño de ovejas. {{plural_you:Velen|Velad}} por ese pueblo porque {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} hacerlo, no porque {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que hacerlo. Eso es lo que Dios quiere. No lo {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} para ganar dinero; {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}} de todo corazón. \v 3 No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} mandones con la gente que Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado para cuidar. Al contrario, con {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de vivir, {{plural_you:muéstrenles|mostradles}} cómo deben vivir ellos.

fr.L: J’exhorte donc les anciens qui sont parmi vous, moi, ancien avec [eux], témoin des souffrances du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} et aussi participant de la gloire qui va être révélée : \v 2 paissez le troupeau de Dieu qui [est] parmi vous, en veillant [sur lui], non par contrainte, mais de bon gré, selon Dieu, ni pour un gain honteux, mais avec empressement, \v 3 ni en dominant sur ceux [qui vous ont été] attribués, mais en devenant des modèles pour le troupeau.
fr.B: J’adresse donc un appel aux anciens qui sont parmi vous. Je suis ancien comme eux, témoin des souffrances du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, et j’aurai part, moi aussi, à la gloire qui va être révélée. \v 2 Prenez soin du troupeau de Dieu qui est parmi vous, comme le font les bergers. Veillez sur lui de bon cœur, comme Dieu le veut, et non par contrainte ; non pour gagner de l’argent, mais avec joie et empressement. \v 3 Ne dominez pas durement sur ceux qui vous ont été confiés ; soyez plutôt des modèles pour le troupeau.
fr.R: Moi aussi, je suis un ancien, et j’ai quelque chose à demander aux anciens qui sont parmi vous. Je suis témoin des souffrances du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, et j’aurai aussi une part de la gloire que Dieu va bientôt montrer. \v 2 Prenez soin du peuple de Dieu comme un berger prend soin d’un troupeau de moutons. Veillez sur lui parce que vous le voulez, et non parce que vous y êtes obligés. C’est ce que Dieu veut. Ne le faites pas pour gagner de l’argent, mais faites-le de tout votre cœur. \v 3 Ne soyez pas autoritaires avec ceux que Dieu vous a confiés. Au contraire, montrez-leur par votre manière de vivre comment ils doivent vivre.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo nawahimiza wazee walio miongoni mwenu, mimi ambaye ni mzee pamoja [nao], tena shahidi wa mateso ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na pia mshiriki wa utukufu unaokaribia kufunuliwa: \v 2 chungeni kundi la Mungu [lililo] kati yenu, mkiliangalia si kwa kushurutishwa bali kwa moyo wa kupenda, kulingana na [mapenzi ya] Mungu; wala si kwa tamaa ya faida mbaya, bali kwa ari; \v 3 wala si kama watu wanaowatawala kwa mabavu wale [mliogawiwa], bali mkiwa vielelezo kwa kundi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nawaomba wazee walio miongoni mwenu. Mimi pia ni mzee kama wao, shahidi wa mateso ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na mmoja atakayeshiriki utukufu ambao uko karibu kufunuliwa. \v 2 Lichungeni kundi la Mungu lililo kati yenu kama wachungaji. Litunzeni kwa hiari yenu, kama Mungu anavyotaka, wala si kwa sababu mmelazimishwa; si ili mjipatie fedha, bali kwa moyo wa kupenda na kwa utayari. \v 3 Msiwatawale kwa ukali watu mliokabidhiwa; badala yake, mwe kielelezo ambacho kundi litakifuata.
sw.R: Mimi pia ni mzee, na nina jambo la kuwaomba wazee walio kati yenu. Mimi ni shahidi wa mateso ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na nitashiriki pia utukufu ambao Mungu yuko karibu kuuonyesha. \v 2 Watunzeni watu wa Mungu kama mchungaji anavyotunza kundi lake la kondoo. Waangalieni kwa sababu mnataka, si kwa sababu mnalazimika. Hivyo ndivyo Mungu anavyotaka. Msifanye kazi hiyo ili kupata pesa, bali ifanyeni kwa moyo wote. \v 3 Msiwe watawala wakali juu ya watu ambao Mungu amewakabidhi ili mwatunze. Badala yake, waonyesheni kwa maisha yenu jinsi wanavyopaswa kuishi.

decisions.choice: elders: the leaders of the churches, and Peter one of them
decisions.reason: πρεσβύτερος can mean an older man, but here the elders are told to shepherd and watch over the flock, which is the work of church leaders (Acts 14:23; 20:17, 28). Peter calls himself συμπρεσβύτερος, a fellow elder: he speaks to them as one of them, not only as an apostle (1:1).

decisions.choice: a witness of the sufferings of Christ: one who saw them and who now tells of them
alternatives: one who shares Christ's sufferings by suffering himself
decisions.reason: μάρτυς is a witness, someone who has seen and testifies to what he saw (Acts 1:8; 2:32). Peter was with Jesus on the night of his arrest (Mark 14:54). The letter often joins Christ's sufferings with glory to follow (1:11; 4:13), and so does this verse.

decisions.choice: a sharer in the glory about to be revealed: Peter will share the glory to be shown when Christ appears
decisions.reason: κοινωνός is a partner, someone who has a share. The glory is "about to be revealed", that is, at Christ's coming (1:5, 1:7; 4:13). The same hope is held out to the elders in verse 4.

decisions.choice: shepherd the flock: the picture of God's people as a flock, and perhaps Jesus' charge to Peter
alternatives: a general picture, with no echo
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures God's people are his flock and their leaders his shepherds, who are judged for feeding themselves instead of the sheep (Ezekiel 34:1-16). Jesus told Peter to shepherd his sheep with the same verb (John 21:15-17). The flock belongs to God, not to the elders.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: with "watching over [it]" and with "according to God"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Some important early manuscripts (among them Codex Sinaiticus as first written and Codex Vaticanus) lack the participle for watching over, and many later manuscripts lack "according to God". Codex Vaticanus also lacks verse 3. None of these changes the sense of the passage. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: according to God: the way God wants, as God himself cares for his people
decisions.reason: κατὰ θεόν means in keeping with God, by his standard (compare 4:6; 2 Corinthians 7:9-10). Willing care is the kind of care God gives.

decisions.choice: for shameful gain: out of greed for money
decisions.reason: αἰσχροκερδῶς is "for base profit". Church leaders could receive support and handle gifts (1 Timothy 5:17-18), and the same fault is ruled out for overseers and deacons (1 Timothy 3:3, 3:8; Titus 1:7).

decisions.choice: the allotted [portions]: the believers given into each elder's care
alternatives: the clergy (a meaning the word gained much later)
decisions.reason: κλῆρος is a lot or a share assigned by lot. Here the plural stands in parallel with "the flock": the groups of believers allotted to the elders. To lord it over them, κατακυριεύω, is to rule them by force, as Jesus said the rulers of the nations do (Mark 10:42).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: several sentences, with each command as its own sentence
alternatives: one sentence, as the Greek has it
decisions.reason: The Greek is one sentence with a string of participles and contrasts. Balanced and Readable break it up and make the participles into commands so that each one is clear.

decisions.choice: the glory that God is about to show
alternatives: the glory about to be revealed
decisions.reason: The passive "to be revealed" implies that God reveals it; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: rule harshly over (B); be bossy with (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lording it over". Balanced and Readable use plain words for ruling by force (m8).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Peter writes to the churches in the plural throughout the letter. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Paul's letters.

decisions.choice: a los ancianos ... los exhorto [yo]
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "elders" first for emphasis. Spanish can keep that order by repeating the object as "los" after the verb, which is ordinary Spanish and needs no brackets.

decisions.choice: les anciens; ancien avec eux (L), ancien comme eux (B), un ancien (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for the leaders of the churches, at every level as in English (m1). "Ancien" also keeps the sense of age that 5:5 plays on.

decisions.choice: mzee pamoja [nao] (L); mzee kama wao (B)
decisions.reason: Peter first speaks of the elders in the third person and then turns to them with commands. Swahili "nawahimiza" / "nawaomba" can mean either "I urge you" or "I urge them", so it covers both, and "fellow elder" is said with reference to the elders as "them".

source.text: καὶ φανερωθέντος τοῦ ἀρχιποίμενος κομιεῖσθε τὸν ἀμαράντινον τῆς δόξης στέφανον.

records.literal_gloss: And having been manifested the chief-shepherd, you will receive the unfading of the glory crown.

en.L: And at the appearing of the Chief Shepherd, you will receive the never-fading crown of glory.
en.B: Then when the Chief Shepherd is revealed, you will be given a crown of glory that will never wither.
en.R: Then when Jesus, the Chief Shepherd, comes back, you will receive a crown of glory. It is a prize that will never wither away.

es.L: Y cuando se manifieste el Pastor principal, {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} la corona de gloria que no se marchita.
es.B: Entonces, cuando aparezca el Pastor principal, se {{plural_you:les|os}} dará una corona de gloria que jamás se marchitará.
es.R: Así, cuando Jesús, el Pastor principal, regrese, {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} una corona de gloria. Es un premio que nunca se marchitará.

fr.L: Et lorsque le Chef des bergers aura paru, vous recevrez la couronne de gloire qui ne se flétrit pas.
fr.B: Alors, quand le Chef des bergers sera révélé, vous recevrez une couronne de gloire qui ne se fanera jamais.
fr.R: Alors, quand Jésus, le Chef des bergers, reviendra, vous recevrez une couronne de gloire. C’est un prix qui ne se fanera jamais.

sw.L: Na Mchungaji Mkuu akiisha kudhihirishwa, mtapokea taji la utukufu lisilonyauka.
sw.B: Kisha Mchungaji Mkuu atakapofunuliwa, mtapewa taji la utukufu ambalo halitanyauka kamwe.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu, Mchungaji Mkuu, atakaporudi, mtapokea taji la utukufu. Ni zawadi ambayo haitanyauka kamwe.

decisions.choice: the Chief Shepherd: Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: ἀρχιποίμην is the head shepherd over the other shepherds. The letter has already called Christ "the shepherd and overseer of your souls" (2:25). The elders are under-shepherds of his flock.

decisions.choice: when he appears: Christ's coming at the end
decisions.reason: φανερόω is to make visible. Christ, now unseen (1:8), will be revealed (1:7, 1:13; 4:13). The same verb is used of his first coming in 1:20.

decisions.choice: the never-fading crown: a victor's wreath that will not wither
decisions.reason: στέφανος was the wreath of leaves given to the winner at the games or to an honored citizen; it soon dried up (1 Corinthians 9:25). ἀμαράντινος, "of amaranth", is a flower name used for what never fades. The same hope is "unfading" in 1:4.

decisions.choice: crown of glory: the crown that is glory itself
decisions.reason: The genitive most likely says what the crown is: the reward is the glory that Peter has just said he will share (verse 1).

decisions.choice: Jesus, the Chief Shepherd, comes back
decisions.reason: Readable names who the Chief Shepherd is (m1) and says what his appearing is (m2).

decisions.choice: el Pastor principal
decisions.reason: The older Spanish "Príncipe de los pastores" is familiar, but the Greek word is simply the chief shepherd. "Pastor principal" keeps the shepherd picture and matches "Pastor" for Christ in 2:25.

decisions.choice: le Chef des bergers
decisions.reason: "Pasteur" today names a church minister, and "le Berger en chef" is not natural French. "Le Chef des bergers" keeps the shepherd picture of 5:2 and of 2:25 in plain words.

decisions.choice: taji la utukufu lisilonyauka
decisions.reason: "Taji" takes either class 5 or class 9 agreement; class 5 ("taji la ... lisilonyauka") is used here. "Kunyauka" is what leaves and flowers do when they wither, which is the picture of the Greek (m3).

records.literal_gloss: Likewise, younger [ones], be subject to elders.

en.L: Likewise, younger ones, be subject to elders.
en.B: In the same way, you who are younger, submit to the elders.
en.R: In the same way, you who are younger must follow the lead of the elders.

es.B: Del mismo modo, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los más jóvenes, {{plural_you:sométanse|someteos}} a los ancianos.
es.R: De la misma manera, los que {{plural_you:son|sois}} más jóvenes {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} seguir la guía de los ancianos.

fr.L: De même, vous, les plus jeunes, soyez soumis aux anciens.
fr.B: De même, vous qui êtes plus jeunes, soumettez-vous aux anciens.
fr.R: De la même façon, vous qui êtes plus jeunes, vous devez suivre la direction des anciens.

sw.B: Hali kadhalika, ninyi mlio vijana, wanyenyekeeni wazee.
sw.R: Vilevile, ninyi mlio vijana mnapaswa kufuata uongozi wa wazee.

decisions.choice: younger ones: the younger members of the church
alternatives: a group of younger church helpers
decisions.reason: νεώτεροι is masculine plural, which Greek also uses for mixed groups. They are set beside the elders, so the command probably speaks to the younger believers generally. Some take it to mean the young men only, as in Titus 2:6.

decisions.choice: elders: the church leaders of verse 1, who are also mostly older
decisions.reason: The same word was used for the leaders in verse 1, and it is not likely to change meaning in so short a space. But it is set against "younger", so the plain sense of age is present as well.

decisions.choice: be subject: accept their leadership
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσω is to take one's place under someone. The letter uses it for every believer's place in society, household and marriage (2:13, 2:18; 3:1). "Likewise" joins this command to those.

decisions.choice: younger ones (L); you who are younger (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording leaves open whether women are included, as the Greek does (m1).

decisions.choice: someterse
decisions.reason: The same verb as in the commands to submit in 2:13, 2:18 and 3:1, and as in Ephesians 5, so the reader can see that "likewise" joins this command to those (m3).

decisions.choice: les plus jeunes
decisions.reason: "Jeunes gens" would suggest young men; like the English, the wording leaves open whether women are included, as the Greek does (m1).

decisions.choice: kunyenyekea
decisions.reason: "Kunyenyekea" is the verb used for this Greek word in Ephesians 5 and in 1 Peter 2-3. "Kutii" (obey) would narrow the sense to doing what one is told (m3).

source.text: πάντες δὲ ἀλλήλοις τὴν ταπεινοφροσύνην ἐγκομβώσασθε, ὅτι Ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν.

records.literal_gloss: All and to one another the humility tie on, because the God proud [ones] opposes, to humble [ones] but gives grace.

en.L: And all [of you], tie on humility toward one another, because “God sets {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} against [the] arrogant, but to [the] lowly {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace.”
en.B: And all of you, tie humility on like a garment in your dealings with one another, because “God stands against the arrogant, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace to the humble.”
en.R: All of you must be humble with each other, as if you were putting on humility like clothes. For “God is against proud people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace to humble people.”

es.L: Y todos [{{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}], {{plural_you:cíñanse|ceñíos}} la humildad unos para con otros, porque «Dios se opone a [los] soberbios, pero da gracia a [los] humildes».
es.B: Y todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, en el trato de unos con otros, {{plural_you:cíñanse|ceñíos}} la humildad como una prenda, porque «Dios se pone en contra de los soberbios, pero a los humildes les da gracia».
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes deben|Vosotros debéis}} ser humildes unos con otros, como si {{plural_you:se vistieran|os vistierais}} de humildad. Porque «Dios lucha contra los orgullosos, pero a los humildes les da gracia».

fr.L: Et tous, nouez sur vous l’humilité les uns envers les autres, car « Dieu s’oppose aux arrogants, mais aux humbles {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne la grâce ».
fr.B: Et vous tous, dans vos relations les uns avec les autres, revêtez-vous d’humilité comme d’un vêtement bien noué, car « Dieu se dresse contre les arrogants, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce aux humbles ».
fr.R: Vous tous, soyez humbles les uns avec les autres, comme si vous mettiez l’humilité sur vous comme un vêtement. Car « Dieu est contre les orgueilleux, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce aux humbles ».

sw.L: Na nyote, mmoja kwa mwingine, jifungieni unyenyekevu, kwa sababu "Mungu anajipanga dhidi ya wenye kiburi, lakini wanyenyekevu anawapa neema."
sw.B: Na ninyi nyote, mnapohusiana ninyi kwa ninyi, jifungieni unyenyekevu kama vazi, kwa sababu "Mungu anasimama dhidi ya wenye kiburi, lakini wanyenyekevu anawapa neema."
sw.R: Nyote mnapaswa kuwa wanyenyekevu ninyi kwa ninyi, kana kwamba mnavaa unyenyekevu kama nguo. Kwa maana "Mungu anapigana na watu wenye kiburi, lakini anawapa neema watu wanyenyekevu."

decisions.choice: tie on: put on as a garment that is knotted in place
alternatives: simply "put on", with no particular garment in mind
decisions.reason: ἐγκομβόομαι comes from a word for a knot or band. It pictures a garment tied on, and some think of the apron a slave tied on for work, which would recall Jesus tying on a towel to wash his disciples' feet (John 13:4-5). The verb is rare, so how far to press the picture is uncertain.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Proverbs 3:34
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek translation of Proverbs 3:34 (the Septuagint), which has "Lord" where Peter has "God". The Hebrew reads that he scorns the scorners but gives favor to the humble; in context "he" is the LORD. James 4:6 quotes the verse in the same form as Peter.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "toward one another" without "being subject"
alternatives: "being subject to one another, tie on humility"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a participle meaning "being subject" after "one another", linking this to the command just given. The shorter text is found in the early manuscripts. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the arrogant and the lowly: those who set themselves above others, and those who do not
decisions.reason: ὑπερήφανος is one who shows himself above others; ταπεινός is low, humble. The humility God rewards is the humility asked for in this verse (compare 3:8).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God. The Greek has no pronoun; English needs one to repeat the subject.

decisions.choice: tie humility on like a garment (B); putting on humility like clothes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture of clothing but do not name the apron, since that detail is uncertain (m1).

decisions.choice: the quotation worded as in James 4:6
decisions.reason: Peter and James quote Proverbs 3:34 in the same Greek form (m2), so the Spanish quotation has the same words at each level as James 4:6. Spanish needs no pronoun for God before "da", so there is no deity_pronoun span here.

decisions.choice: cíñanse la humildad
decisions.reason: "Ceñirse" is to tie something around oneself, close to the Greek picture of a garment knotted in place (m1).

decisions.choice: the quotation worded as in James 4:6
decisions.reason: Peter and James quote Proverbs 3:34 in the same Greek form (m2), so the Swahili quotation has the same words at each level as James 4:6. The pronoun for God is carried by the verb ("anawapa"), so there is no span.

decisions.choice: jifungieni unyenyekevu
decisions.reason: "Kujifungia" is to tie something on oneself, which keeps the picture of a garment knotted in place (m1).

source.text: Ταπεινώθητε οὖν ὑπὸ τὴν κραταιὰν χεῖρα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα ὑμᾶς ὑψώσῃ ἐν καιρῷ, πᾶσαν τὴν μέριμναν ὑμῶν ἐπιρίψαντες ἐπ’ αὐτόν, ὅτι αὐτῷ μέλει περὶ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Be humbled therefore under the mighty hand of the God, so that you he may lift up in [due] time, \v 7 all the worry of you having thrown upon him, because to him it is a concern about you.

en.L: Be humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may lift you up in [due] time, \v 7 throwing all your worry onto {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because you are a concern to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Humble yourselves, then, under God's powerful hand, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may raise you up when the time is right. \v 7 Do this by throwing every worry you have onto {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because you matter to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: So bow down humbly under God's powerful hand. Then, when the time is right, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lift you up. \v 7 Hand all your worries over to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cares about you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Humíllense|Humillaos}}, pues, bajo la mano poderosa de Dios, para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} levante en [el] tiempo [debido], \v 7 arrojando sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} toda {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} preocupación, porque {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:importan|importáis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Humíllense|Humillaos}}, entonces, bajo la mano poderosa de Dios, para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} levante cuando llegue el momento. \v 7 {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} echando sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} toda preocupación que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}}, porque {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:importan|importáis}}.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:inclínense|inclinaos}} con humildad bajo la mano poderosa de Dios. Entonces, cuando llegue el momento, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} levantará. \v 7 {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} manos todas {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} preocupaciones, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se preocupa por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Soyez donc abaissés sous la main puissante de Dieu, afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous élève au temps [voulu], \v 7 jetant sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} toute votre inquiétude, car vous êtes l’objet de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} soins.
fr.B: Abaissez-vous donc sous la main puissante de Dieu, afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous relève au moment voulu. \v 7 Faites-le en vous déchargeant sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de tous vos soucis, car vous comptez pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Alors, inclinez-vous humblement sous la main puissante de Dieu. Ensuite, au bon moment, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous relèvera. \v 7 Confiez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tous vos soucis, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prend soin de vous.

sw.L: Basi mnyenyekezwe chini ya mkono wenye nguvu wa Mungu, ili awainue kwa wakati [ufaao], \v 7 mkimtupia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} wasiwasi wenu wote, kwa sababu mnamhusu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.
sw.B: Basi jinyenyekezeni chini ya mkono wenye nguvu wa Mungu, ili awainue wakati utakapofika. \v 7 Fanyeni hivyo kwa kumtupia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kila wasiwasi mlio nao, kwa sababu ninyi ni wa thamani {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo jishusheni kwa unyenyekevu chini ya mkono wenye nguvu wa Mungu. Kisha, wakati ufaao utakapofika, atawainua. \v 7 Mkabidhini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} wasiwasi wenu wote, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anawajali.

decisions.choice: be humbled: accept the low place God gives, and humble yourselves under it
alternatives: only "humble yourselves" as one's own act
decisions.reason: ταπεινώθητε is passive in form: let yourselves be made low. It takes up "the humble" of the quotation just made (verse 5). In this letter the low place includes unjust suffering, which believers are to bear while trusting God (2:19-23; 4:19).

decisions.choice: the mighty hand of God: God's power, both to discipline and to rescue
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures God's mighty hand is his power at work, above all when he brought Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:19-20; Deuteronomy 26:8). The hand that brings them low is the hand that will lift them up.

decisions.choice: in [due] time: at the time God chooses, finally at the end
decisions.reason: καιρός is the fitting or appointed time. The letter looks to salvation "ready to be revealed in the last time" (1:5) and to glory when Christ appears (5:4).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in time"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add a word meaning "of visitation", the phrase used in 2:12. The shorter reading is the one found in most manuscripts, including the earliest. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: throwing all your worry onto him: the way to humble oneself
alternatives: a separate command, "throw all your worry on him"
decisions.reason: ἐπιρίψαντες is a participle hanging on the command "be humbled". It most likely says how they are to humble themselves: the proud carry their own burdens, the humble hand them to God. Some read it as a command in its own right; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: an echo of Psalm 55:23
decisions.reason: The psalm says to throw one's burden on the LORD, who will sustain you (Psalm 55:23; 54:23 in the Septuagint, where the same verb and the word for worry are used). Here the one who takes the worry is God (verse 6).

decisions.choice: it is a concern to him about you: God cares about them
decisions.reason: μέλει is impersonal: something is a care or concern to someone. God is concerned for them; their worry has a place to go.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God.

decisions.choice: Do this by
decisions.reason: Balanced starts a new sentence for verse 7 and supplies "Do this by" to keep the participle tied to the command (m5).

decisions.choice: you are a concern to him (L); you matter to him (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek makes them the subject of God's concern rather than making God the subject of a verb. Literal and Balanced keep that turn; Readable says it in the simplest way, "he cares about you".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} le {{plural_you:importan|importáis}}
decisions.reason: Spanish "importar" has the same shape as the Greek impersonal verb: the readers are the subject and God is the one to whom they matter (m7). Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable says "él se preocupa por ustedes", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Soyez abaissés (L); Abaissez-vous (B)
decisions.reason: French "humilier" now means to shame someone, which is not the sense: the readers are to accept the low place under God's hand (m1). "S’abaisser" says that without the idea of disgrace.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yeye, kwake)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("awainue", "mkimtupia", "anawajali"), and a prefix cannot take a capital. So the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, and Swahili has fewer spans than English.

decisions.choice: mnamhusu yeye
decisions.reason: "Kuhusu" (to concern) lets Swahili keep the Greek turn in which the readers are a concern to God (m7). Balanced says "ninyi ni wa thamani kwake" (you are precious to him), Readable "anawajali" (he cares for you).

en.B: Keep a clear head. Stay awake.

fr.B: Gardez la tête claire. Restez éveillés.
fr.R: Réfléchissez avec clarté et restez vigilants.

decisions.choice: be sober: be clear-headed and in control of yourselves
decisions.reason: νήφω is literally to be free of wine, but in this letter it is a state of mind: ready and clear in thought (1:13; 4:7).

decisions.choice: keep awake: stay watchful
decisions.reason: γρηγορέω is to stay awake, keep watch. Jesus gave this command to Peter and the others in Gethsemane, and they fell asleep (Mark 14:37-38). Here the reason is the enemy who follows.

decisions.choice: Keep a clear head. Stay awake. (B); Think clearly and stay alert. (R)
decisions.reason: "Be sober" can suggest only not drinking; Balanced and Readable name the clear mind that is meant (m1).

source.text: ὁ ἀντίδικος ὑμῶν διάβολος ὡς λέων ὠρυόμενος περιπατεῖ ζητῶν τινα καταπιεῖν·

records.literal_gloss: The opponent of you, devil, like a lion roaring walks about seeking someone to swallow down;

en.L: Your opponent, [the] devil, walks about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to swallow down.
en.B: The devil, your opponent, roams about like a lion that roars, hunting for someone to swallow up.
en.R: The devil is your enemy. Like a hungry lion that roars, he goes around hunting for someone to eat up.

es.L: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} adversario, [el] diablo, anda rondando como un león que ruge, buscando a alguien a quien tragarse.
es.B: El diablo, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} adversario, merodea como un león que ruge, a la caza de alguien a quien tragarse.
es.R: El diablo es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} enemigo. Como un león hambriento que ruge, anda por todas partes buscando a quién comerse.

fr.L: Votre adversaire, le diable, rôde comme un lion rugissant, cherchant quelqu’un à engloutir.
fr.B: Le diable, votre adversaire, rôde comme un lion qui rugit, cherchant quelqu’un à dévorer.
fr.R: Le diable est votre ennemi. Comme un lion affamé qui rugit, il rôde et cherche quelqu’un à manger.

sw.L: Mpinzani wenu, Ibilisi, anatembea huku na huko kama simba anayenguruma, akitafuta mtu wa kummeza.
sw.B: Ibilisi, mpinzani wenu, anazurura kama simba anayenguruma, akiwinda mtu wa kummeza.
sw.R: Ibilisi ni adui yenu. Kama simba mwenye njaa anayenguruma, anazunguka kila mahali akitafuta mtu wa kumla.

decisions.choice: opponent: an enemy, perhaps with the sense of an accuser
decisions.reason: ἀντίδικος is first an opponent in a lawsuit (Matthew 5:25), then any enemy. It fits the name that follows: διάβολος means slanderer, accuser, and is the name of Satan (compare Revelation 12:10).

decisions.choice: like a roaring lion: a picture of a deadly enemy
decisions.reason: In Psalm 22:14 the sufferer's enemies open their mouths against him like a ravening and roaring lion. The devil works through the hostility believers face (4:12-16), and the next verse speaks of their sufferings.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "seeking someone to swallow down"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts begin with "because", joining this to the commands just given. Manuscripts also differ over the last words, which can read "someone to swallow" or "whom he may swallow". The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a hungry lion; to eat up
alternatives: a roaring lion seeking someone to swallow down
decisions.reason: Readable adds "hungry", which the search for prey implies.

decisions.choice: Ibilisi
decisions.reason: The Greek word means the slanderer, the devil (m1). "Ibilisi" is the Swahili word for the devil, as in James 4:7; "Shetani" is kept for the name Satan.

source.text: ᾧ ἀντίστητε στερεοὶ τῇ πίστει, εἰδότες τὰ αὐτὰ τῶν παθημάτων τῇ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ὑμῶν ἀδελφότητι ἐπιτελεῖσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: Whom resist, firm in the faith, knowing the same [kinds] of the sufferings to the in the world of you brotherhood are being accomplished.

en.L: Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that the same [kinds] of sufferings are being accomplished in your {{gender:family of brothers and sisters|brotherhood}} in the world.
en.B: Stand up to him and hold firm in your faith. You know that your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} all over the world are enduring these same sufferings.
en.R: Stand against him and keep your faith strong. Remember that your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} all over the world are suffering in the same way you are.

es.L: {{plural_you:Resístanlo|Resistidlo}}, firmes en la fe, sabiendo que las mismas [clases] de sufrimientos se están llevando a cabo en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} hermandad [que está] en el mundo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Háganle|Hacedle}} frente y {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes en la fe. {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos en todo el mundo están soportando estos mismos sufrimientos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Enfréntense|Enfrentaos}} a él y {{plural_you:mantengan|mantened}} fuerte {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe. {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos en todo el mundo están sufriendo igual que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Résistez-lui, fermes dans la foi, sachant que les mêmes souffrances s’accomplissent dans votre {{gender:famille de frères et sœurs|fraternité}} [qui est] dans le monde.
fr.B: Tenez-lui tête et restez fermes dans votre foi. Vous savez que vos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} dans le monde entier endurent les mêmes souffrances.
fr.R: Opposez-vous à lui et gardez une foi solide. Souvenez-vous que vos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} dans le monde entier souffrent de la même façon que vous.

sw.L: Simameni kinyume naye, imara katika imani, mkijua kwamba [aina] zile zile za mateso zinakamilishwa katika jumuiya ya ndugu zenu iliyo ulimwenguni.
sw.B: Simameni imara dhidi yake, mkiishikilia imani yenu. Mnajua kwamba ndugu zenu kote ulimwenguni wanavumilia mateso hayo hayo.
sw.R: Simameni kidete dhidi yake, na imani yenu iwe na nguvu. Kumbukeni kwamba ndugu zenu kote ulimwenguni wanateseka kama ninyi.

decisions.choice: firm in the faith: standing solid in their trust in God
alternatives: firm in holding to the Christian teaching
decisions.reason: τῇ πίστει most likely says where their firmness lies: in their faith, the trust in God the letter speaks of throughout (1:5, 1:7, 1:9, 1:21). The article can mean "your faith".

decisions.choice: resist: stand against the devil, who then has no power to swallow them
decisions.reason: ἀνθίστημι is to stand against, hold one's ground. James 4:7 gives the same command about the devil, and Ephesians 6:11-13 pictures the believer standing firm against him.

decisions.choice: are being accomplished in your brotherhood: the same sufferings are being borne by believers everywhere
alternatives: are being laid on your brotherhood as a set amount that must be completed
decisions.reason: ἐπιτελέω is to complete or carry out; in the passive with a dative it can mean that something is being undergone by someone. Some see the thought that a measure of suffering is being filled up before the end. The plain point is that they do not suffer alone.

decisions.choice: brotherhood: the whole family of believers
decisions.reason: ἀδελφότης is the community of brothers and sisters, as in 2:17. It includes women and men.

decisions.choice: the world: the whole inhabited world where believers live
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is the world as a place: believers everywhere, not the world opposed to God.

decisions.choice: {{gender:family of brothers and sisters|brotherhood}} (L); {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Gender setting: the word means the whole community (m4).

decisions.choice: Stand up to him (B); Stand against him (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for holding one's ground against an attacker.

decisions.choice: hermandad (L); hermanos (B, R), no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans and Philippians, Spanish "hermandad" and "hermanos" already take in the whole community of believers, women and men (m4), so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: jumuiya ya ndugu (L); ndugu (B, R), no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters (m4), so Swahili needs no gender span; the only traditional alternative would add "wa kiume" (male) and change the meaning.

source.text: ὁ δὲ θεὸς πάσης χάριτος, ὁ καλέσας ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν αἰώνιον αὐτοῦ δόξαν ἐν Χριστῷ, ὀλίγον παθόντας αὐτὸς καταρτίσει, στηρίξει, σθενώσει, θεμελιώσει.

records.literal_gloss: The but God of all grace, the [one] having called you into the eternal of him glory in Christ, a little [while] having suffered, he himself will restore, will establish, will strengthen, will found.

en.L: And the God of all grace, who called you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eternal glory in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, after you have suffered a little [while], will {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} restore, make firm, strengthen, [and] ground [you].
en.B: And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eternal glory in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, will {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} restore you, make you firm and strong, and set you on a sure foundation.
en.R: You will suffer for only a little while. Then God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will make you whole again. He will make you strong and steady and give you a firm place to stand. All grace comes from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and through {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called you to share {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eternal glory.

es.L: Y el Dios de toda gracia, que {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria eterna en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, después de que {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} sufrido un poco [de tiempo], {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo [{{plural_you:los|os}}] restaurará, consolidará, fortalecerá [y] cimentará.
es.B: Y cuando {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} padecido por un breve tiempo, el Dios de toda gracia, que {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria eterna en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, será {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo quien {{plural_you:los|os}} restaure, {{plural_you:les|os}} dé firmeza y fuerza, y {{plural_you:los|os}} asiente sobre un fundamento seguro.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes sufrirán|Vosotros sufriréis}} solo por poco tiempo. Luego Dios mismo {{plural_you:los|os}} restaurará por completo. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} dará fuerza y firmeza, y un lugar seguro donde estar de pie. Toda gracia viene de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y por medio {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ha llamado a compartir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria eterna.

fr.L: Et le Dieu de toute grâce, qui vous a appelés à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire éternelle {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, après que vous aurez souffert un peu [de temps], {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} [vous] rétablira, [vous] affermira, [vous] fortifiera, [vous] fondera.
fr.B: Et après que vous aurez souffert un peu de temps, le Dieu de toute grâce, qui vous a appelés à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire éternelle {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, vous rétablira {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, vous rendra fermes et forts, et vous établira sur un fondement solide.
fr.R: Vous ne souffrirez que peu de temps. Ensuite, Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous rétablira complètement. Il vous rendra forts et solides, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donnera un endroit ferme où vous tenir. Toute grâce vient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a appelés à partager {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire éternelle.

sw.L: Na Mungu wa neema zote, ambaye aliwaita kwenye utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa milele katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, baada ya ninyi kuteseka kwa muda mfupi, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe atawarejesha, atawasimika imara, atawapa nguvu, [na] kuwaweka juu ya msingi.
sw.B: Baada ya kuteseka kwa muda mfupi, Mungu wa neema zote, aliyewaita kwenye utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa milele katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe atawarejesha, atawafanya imara na wenye nguvu, na kuwasimika juu ya msingi thabiti.
sw.R: Mtateseka kwa muda mfupi tu. Kisha Mungu mwenyewe atawafanya wazima tena. Atawapa nguvu na uthabiti, na mahali imara pa kusimama. Neema yote inatoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, na kupitia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amewaita mshiriki utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa milele.

decisions.choice: the God of all grace: the God who gives grace of every kind
decisions.reason: The genitive describes God by what he gives. The letter speaks of God's grace in its many forms (4:10) and of the grace still to be brought at Christ's coming (1:13).

decisions.choice: in Christ: God called them through Christ, into glory they share in him
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "called" or with "glory". Both are true in the letter (1:3; 5:14), and the order of the words allows both.

decisions.choice: restore, make firm, strengthen, ground: God will make them whole and stable
decisions.reason: καταρτίζω is to put in order, mend, as fishermen mended nets (Mark 1:19); στηρίζω is to make firm, the word Jesus used when he told Peter to strengthen his brothers (Luke 22:32); σθενόω is to give strength; θεμελιόω is to set on a foundation. The four together promise lasting stability after suffering.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "called you", "in Christ", four promises in the future tense
alternatives: a prayer: "may he restore, establish, strengthen"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ at several points in this verse. Some read "us" for "you"; many add "Jesus"; many later manuscripts have the verbs as a wish ("may he restore ..."), not a promise; and some important early manuscripts lack the last verb, "ground". Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a little while: short compared with eternal glory
decisions.reason: ὀλίγον recalls 1:6: "for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved". The suffering is short beside the glory that is eternal.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}; {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God and the title setting. At the start of a Readable sentence "He" is capitalized either way and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: the short suffering first, then God's work
alternatives: "the God of all grace ... after you have suffered ... will restore"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "after you have suffered" first so that the long description of God does not separate him from what he will do. Readable gives the description of God its own sentence at the end.

decisions.choice: restore you, make you firm and strong, set you on a sure foundation (B); make you whole again, strong and steady, a firm place to stand (R)
decisions.reason: Four short verbs read flatly in English; Balanced and Readable keep all four ideas in plainer phrases (m3).

decisions.choice: Mungu wa neema zote
decisions.reason: "Neema" has the same form in the singular and the plural, and the plural agreement "zote" says "grace of every kind", which is how the meaning decision reads the phrase (m1). Readable says "Neema yote inatoka kwake" (all grace comes from him).

source.text: αὐτῷ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.

records.literal_gloss: To him the might into the ages of the ages; amen.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [is] the might for the ages of the ages. Amen.
en.B: Power belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forever and ever. Amen.
en.R: He rules with power forever and ever. Amen.

es.L: A {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [pertenece] el dominio por los siglos de los siglos. Amén.
es.B: El poder {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pertenece por siempre jamás. Amén.
es.R: Él reina con poder para siempre. Amén.

fr.L: À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} [est] la puissance aux siècles des siècles. Amen.
fr.B: La puissance {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartient pour toujours et à jamais. Amen.
fr.R: Il règne avec puissance pour toujours et à jamais. Amen.

sw.L: Kwake [ni] uweza hadi nyakati za nyakati. Amina.
sw.B: Uweza ni {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} milele na milele. Amina.
sw.R: Yeye anatawala kwa nguvu milele na milele. Amina.

decisions.choice: to him is the might: a statement of praise
alternatives: a wish: "to him be the might"
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. In the similar praise in 4:11 Peter writes "is", so this is most likely a statement of what is true of God, not a wish. The difference is small.

decisions.choice: might: God's ruling power
decisions.reason: κράτος is power that rules and prevails, the power of the mighty hand in verse 6. It answers the threat of the devil (verse 8).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the might"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the glory and the might", the fuller wording of 4:11. The shorter text has strong early support. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun for God. Readable begins with "He", capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: forever and ever
alternatives: for the ages of the ages
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom means without end; Literal keeps its form.

decisions.choice: [pertenece]
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb, and the meaning decision reads it as a statement (m1). Spanish "sea" would make it a wish, so Literal supplies "pertenece".

source.text: Διὰ Σιλουανοῦ ὑμῖν τοῦ πιστοῦ ἀδελφοῦ, ὡς λογίζομαι, δι’ ὀλίγων ἔγραψα, παρακαλῶν καὶ ἐπιμαρτυρῶν ταύτην εἶναι ἀληθῆ χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰς ἣν στῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: Through Silvanus to you, the faithful brother, as I reckon, through few [words] I wrote, urging and testifying this to be true grace of the God; into which stand.

en.L: Through Silvanus, the faithful brother, as I reckon [him], I wrote to you in few [words], urging and testifying this to be the true grace of God, in which stand [firm].
en.B: I have written you this short letter through Silvanus, whom I count a faithful brother. I write to encourage you and to testify that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.
en.R: Silvanus, whom I trust as a faithful brother, has helped me with this short letter to you. I wrote to encourage you and to tell you plainly that this is God's true grace. Hold on to it and stand firm.

es.L: Por medio de Silvano, el hermano fiel, según [mi] juicio, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí en pocas [palabras], animándo{{plural_you:los|os}} y dando testimonio de que esta es la verdadera gracia de Dios, en la cual {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} [firmes].
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he escrito esta carta breve por medio de Silvano, hermano fiel según mi propio juicio. Mi propósito es dar{{plural_you:les|os}} ánimo y dar testimonio de que esta es la verdadera gracia de Dios. {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} firmes en ella.
es.R: Silvano, en quien confío como hermano fiel, me ha ayudado con esta carta breve para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} escribí para dar{{plural_you:les|os}} ánimo y para decir{{plural_you:les|os}} con claridad que esta es la verdadera gracia de Dios. {{plural_you:Aférrense|Aferraos}} a ella y {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes.

fr.L: Par Silvain, le frère fidèle, à ce que je pense, je vous ai écrit en peu [de mots], exhortant et attestant que c’est là la vraie grâce de Dieu, dans laquelle tenez [ferme].
fr.B: Je vous ai écrit cette courte lettre par l’intermédiaire de Silvain, que je considère comme un frère fidèle. Je vous écris pour vous encourager et pour attester que c’est bien là la vraie grâce de Dieu. Tenez-y ferme.
fr.R: Silvain, en qui j’ai confiance comme en un frère fidèle, m’a aidé pour cette courte lettre que je vous envoie. Je vous ai écrit pour vous encourager et pour vous dire clairement que c’est là la vraie grâce de Dieu. Restez-y attachés et tenez bon.

sw.L: Kupitia Silwano, ndugu mwaminifu, kwa jinsi ninavyomwona, nimewaandikia kwa [maneno] machache, nikiwatia moyo na kuwathibitishia kwamba neema hii ni neema ya kweli ya Mungu; ndani yake simameni [imara].
sw.B: Nimewaandikia barua hii fupi kupitia Silwano, ambaye namhesabu kuwa ndugu mwaminifu. Naandika ili kuwatia moyo na kushuhudia kwamba neema hii ni neema ya kweli ya Mungu. Simameni imara ndani yake.
sw.R: Silwano, ambaye ninamtegemea kama ndugu mwaminifu, amenisaidia katika barua hii fupi kwenu. Niliandika ili kuwatia moyo na kuwaambia waziwazi kwamba hii ni neema ya kweli ya Mungu. Ishikeni na msimame imara ndani yake.

decisions.choice: through Silvanus: Silvanus helped write the letter, or carried it, or both
alternatives: Silvanus as the one who carried the letter only
Silvanus as the one who wrote it down only
decisions.reason: "Writing through" someone could name the one who carried a letter to its readers (compare Acts 15:23, where the letter is sent "by their hand"), and also the one who helped write it. The words do not say which, and both may be true.

decisions.choice: Silvanus: very probably the Silas of Acts, Paul's companion
decisions.reason: A Silvanus is named with Paul in 1 Thessalonians 1:1, 2 Thessalonians 1:1 and 2 Corinthians 1:19, and Acts calls Paul's companion Silas, a leader of the Jerusalem church (Acts 15:22, 15:40). Silvanus is the fuller, Latin form of the name. The letter does not say they are the same man, but it is very likely.

decisions.choice: as I reckon: Peter's own judgment that Silvanus is faithful
decisions.reason: ὡς λογίζομαι most likely goes with "the faithful brother": Peter commends him. It is not a doubt; it is a firm judgment (compare Romans 8:18).

decisions.choice: this is the true grace of God: what the letter has set out, suffering included, is God's real grace to them
decisions.reason: ταύτην points back over the letter: the hope, the new birth and the call to suffer as Christ did. Peter has said that suffering unjustly is grace before God (2:19-20).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: a command, "stand [firm] in it"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "in which you stand", a statement like Romans 5:2. The command has strong early support. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: three sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable divide the sentence at its natural joints and make the closing relative clause a command of its own.

decisions.choice: has helped me with this short letter
decisions.reason: Readable keeps open what Silvanus did (m1).

decisions.choice: Silvain
decisions.reason: The usual French form of the name, as in the Pauline letters; the English keeps "Silvanus" rather than "Silas" for the same reason, since the identification is a meaning decision (m2), not a rendering.

decisions.choice: amenisaidia katika barua hii
decisions.reason: "Kuandika" would say that Silvanus helped write the letter. "Katika barua hii" (with this letter) keeps open whether he helped write it, carried it, or both (m1).

source.text: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτὴ καὶ Μᾶρκος ὁ υἱός μου.

records.literal_gloss: Greets you the [one] in Babylon chosen-together and Mark the son of me.

en.L: She who is in Babylon, chosen together [with you], greets you, and [so does] Mark my son.
en.B: She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, and so does my son Mark.
en.R: The church here in Babylon sends you greetings. God chose them, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose you. My son Mark also greets you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} saluda la [que está] en Babilonia, elegida junto [con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}], y Marcos, mi hijo.
es.B: La que está en Babilonia, elegida junto con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} envía saludos, y también mi hijo Marcos.
es.R: La iglesia de aquí, en Babilonia, {{plural_you:les|os}} envía saludos. Dios los eligió a ellos, igual que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Mi hijo Marcos también {{plural_you:los|os}} saluda.

fr.L: Celle qui est à Babylone, élue avec [vous], vous salue, et Marc, mon fils.
fr.B: Celle qui est à Babylone, élue avec vous, vous envoie ses salutations, ainsi que mon fils Marc.
fr.R: L’église qui est ici à Babylone vous envoie ses salutations. Dieu l’a choisie, tout comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a choisis. Mon fils Marc vous salue aussi.

sw.L: Anawasalimu [yule] aliye Babeli, mteule pamoja [nanyi], na Marko mwanangu.
sw.B: Yule aliye Babeli, aliyechaguliwa pamoja nanyi, anawasalimu, na vivyo hivyo mwanangu Marko.
sw.R: Kanisa la hapa Babeli linawasalimu. Mungu aliwachagua wao, kama alivyowachagua ninyi. Mwanangu Marko pia anawasalimu.

decisions.choice: she who is chosen together with you: the church where Peter is
decisions.reason: The Greek is feminine: "the co-chosen [one]". The word for church is feminine, and the letter calls its readers chosen (1:1; 2:9), so a church sending greetings to churches fits best (compare 2 John 1, 13). Peter was married (1 Corinthians 9:5), and some have read this as his wife. Some manuscripts add the word for church.

decisions.choice: Babylon: where Peter is when he writes; most likely a name for Rome
alternatives: the old city of Babylon in Mesopotamia
a Roman fort named Babylon in Egypt
decisions.reason: Babylon was where God's people were taken into exile. The letter calls its readers exiles and strangers (1:1, 1:17; 2:11), and Revelation uses Babylon as a name for Rome (Revelation 14:8; 17:5, 18). Christian tradition from the second century places Peter in Rome at the end of his life. There is no record of Peter in the eastern Babylon, though a name taken literally is possible.

decisions.choice: Mark my son: Mark, Peter's son in the faith
decisions.reason: "Son" is used of a younger believer one has taught, as Paul calls Timothy his child (1 Timothy 1:2). This is very probably John Mark, whose mother's house Peter went to in Jerusalem (Acts 12:12), who later worked with Barnabas and Paul (Acts 12:25; 15:37-39; Colossians 4:10; Philemon 24).

decisions.choice: She who is in Babylon, chosen together [with you]
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Greek's feminine figure, so that the reader can see the open question (m1).

decisions.choice: The church here in Babylon; God chose them, just as he chose you
alternatives: She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you
decisions.reason: Readable names the church (m1), adds "here" because the greeting comes from where Peter is, and spells out "chosen together".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun for God in Readable's expansion.

decisions.choice: L’église qui est ici à Babylone; Dieu l’a choisie
decisions.reason: One congregation is meant, so the term sheet's lowercase "l’église". The feminine noun lets French keep the feminine of the Greek in "l’a choisie", where the English says "them".

decisions.choice: yule aliye Babeli
decisions.reason: The Greek is feminine (m1), but Swahili pronouns and verb prefixes have no gender, so "yule aliye Babeli" cannot show it. Adding "mwanamke" (woman) would decide for Peter's wife, and "kanisa" would decide for the church; Literal and Balanced leave the question open, and Readable names the church as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: Greet one another in a kiss of love.

en.L: Greet one another in a kiss of love.
en.B: Greet each other with a loving kiss.
en.R: Greet each other with a kiss to show your love for one another.

es.L: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} unos a otros con un beso de amor.
es.B: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} los unos a los otros con un beso lleno de amor.
es.R: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} con un beso, para mostrar{{plural_you:se|os}} el amor que {{plural_you:se tienen|os tenéis}}.

fr.L: Saluez-vous les uns les autres par un baiser d’amour.
fr.B: Saluez-vous les uns les autres par un baiser affectueux.
fr.R: Saluez-vous les uns les autres par un baiser, pour montrer que vous vous aimez.

sw.B: Salimianeni ninyi kwa ninyi kwa busu lenye upendo.
sw.R: Salimianeni kwa busu kuonyesha kwamba mnapendana.

decisions.choice: a kiss of love: the greeting of family members, shared among believers
decisions.reason: A kiss was a usual greeting among relatives and close friends. Believers greeted one another as family (Romans 16:16; 1 Corinthians 16:20, where it is "a holy kiss"). Here it is named for the love the letter has urged on them (1:22; 4:8).

source.text: εἰρήνη ὑμῖν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Peace to you all, the [ones] in Christ.

en.L: Peace [be] to you all, those in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: May all of you who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} have peace.
en.R: May God give peace to all of you who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Paz a todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los [que {{plural_you:están|estáis}}] en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.B: Que todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} paz.
es.R: Que Dios dé paz a todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.

fr.L: Paix à vous tous qui [êtes] {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}.
fr.B: Que la paix soit avec vous tous qui appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Que Dieu donne la paix à vous tous qui appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

sw.L: Amani kwenu ninyi nyote, mlio ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Ninyi nyote mlio wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} na mwe na amani.
sw.R: Mungu awape amani ninyi nyote mlio wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: peace to you: a blessing, a prayer for God's peace
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb; it is a wish, as at the start of the letter (1:2). Peace is wholeness and well-being given by God.

decisions.choice: those in Christ: those joined to Christ, who belong to him
decisions.reason: "In Christ" names believers by their union with him, as in 3:16 and 5:10.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in Christ", with no "Amen"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Jesus", and many add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: May ... have peace (B); May God give peace (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the wish a prayer; Readable says who gives peace (m1).
